text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The ruling Socialist party said it was ready to give up its mandate for forming a new government if the opposition gives guarantees it would form a coalition government within the current parliament with the mandate of the parliamentary minority.
-- Bulgaria is a top priority for financial aid in Russia's 1997 budget, visiting deputy chairman of the Russian Duma Sergei Baburin said.

-- Bulgaria's opposition deputy Muravei Radev proposed in parliament that the monthly untaxable income should be raised to 15,000 levs from 5,500 levs from February 1, twice as much than the outgoing government had suggested.
-- Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions said the minimum monthly salary in the country should be raised to $40 to guarantee the survival of the people.
-- Sofia public transport workers were expected to join the national strike on Monday to support opposition protests against the possible formation of a second Socialist cabinet.
Sofia students were expected to block main intersections in Sofia during the whole day.
-- Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov said he would not hold talks on the formation of a new government until Tuesday when the mandate of the ruling Socialists to form a cabinet expires.
-- Bulgaria's state Bulbank is expected to buy a 34 percent stake in the Central Cooperative Bank (CCB) by the end of the month, CCB executive director Stoyan Alexandrov said.
-- Cumulative inflation for the first quarter was expected at 185 percent, Bulgaria's biggest Confederation of Independent Trade Unions officials said.
